text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet resolved to raise pensions by 19.5 percent from next January, announced state secretary at the Prime Minister's Office Elemer Kiss adding that citizens would be free to have 1 percent of their personal income tax allocated to a foundation, church or social organisation of their own choice from 1998. The premier has convened a conference for November 22 under the title Economy '97.
- President Arpad Goncz arrived in Kiev, Ukraine.
- Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal expressed optimism in Moscow Thursday regarding the return of Hungarian art treasures.
- Tenders will be launched for the purchase of the steelworks Ozdi Acelmuvek and the glass factory St-Glass Rt, based in Salgotarjan.
- Matav is to limit services to 50-70,000 of its most serious debtors.

- A large-scale investigation has been launched amid fears that underworld clashes will continue after a stable owner and amateur horse carriage driver was shot at the Kerepesi ut racing ground Wednesday evening.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The top bodies of the two government coalition parties agreed to jointly outline the key political and legislative tasks for the next 18 months next Monday.
- Free Democrat President Ivan Peto is the sole presidential candidate ahead of next weekend's Free Democrat congress.
- The results of the national oil and gas company MOL Rt. in the first nine months of the year generated a 11.6 billion forint post-tax profit on revenues of 343 billion forints.
- Revenues of Zalakeramia Rt. in the first nine months of 1996 increased by 15.7 percent over the same period last year to 2.87 billion forints.
- Zwack Rt took in gross revenues of 9.8 billion forints in the first nine months of 1996.

- A report on Hungary put together by the Allied forces, published in the French daily Le Figaro Thursday, said that according to the victors in World War II, Nazi Germany looted gold worth $32 million from Hungary between 1938 and 1945.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The interest expenditure of the central budget neared 390 billion forints by late September, according to the State Debt Management Centre. Some 1,018 billion forints of debt was repaid over the first nine months of this year.

- The annual economic growth rate of reform countries is likely to exceed that of countries in the European Union by 3 percent in the long term, said Peter Havlik of the Institute of Comparative Sciences in Vienna yesterday.
- Foreign winners of privatisation tenders for energy firms may be allowed to sell shares to buyers who satisfy certain conditions.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- About 74 percent of companies in the construction industry plan to increase their prices, according to a poll.
- Gross wages went up by 20 percent and 12 percent in the private sector and at budgetary organs respectively in January - September.
- The members of the Budapest Commodity Exchange will decide on November 27 whether to strengthen cooperation with the Budapest Stock Exchange.
